items.t: AbbVie stock: Q3 outlook raised as pipeline advances
sum: AbbVie strengthened its investment case during the week ended Saturday, November 7, with stronger third-quarter results, a higher full-year outlook and two pipeline developments. The company reported the results on October 30, covering the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

According to AbbVie, third-quarter revenue rose 10.3 percent year over year to 17.4 billion US dollars. Adjusted earnings reached 3.82 US dollars per share. AbbVie lifted its 2026 adjusted diluted earnings guidance to 13.95 to 13.99 US dollars per share from 13.76 to 13.96 US dollars and raised its revenue outlook by 200 million US dollars to 67.8 billion US dollars.

The outlook includes an unfavorable 0.69 US dollar per-share impact from acquired in-process research and development and milestone expenses incurred through the third quarter. AbbVie said the guidance excludes similar expenses that may arise after the quarter.

AbbVie also signed an exclusive global license with Nxera for NXE0033744, an investigational EP4 receptor agonist for inflammatory bowel disease. The agreement includes a 100 million US dollar upfront payment and up to 1.37 billion US dollars in development and commercial milestones, plus tiered royalties. The transaction remains subject to customary antitrust clearances, according to Pharmaceutical Executive.

Separately, AbbVie expanded its Oxford research facility in the United Kingdom. The new 12,000-square-foot site supports research in immunology, neuroscience and oncology and forms part of more than 120 million pounds invested and committed across the UK life-sciences ecosystem, the company said in its Oxford announcement.

AbbVie stock traded at 260.65 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:20 CET on Saturday, November 7. Investors will weigh the raised outlook against research spending, milestone costs and the execution risk attached to early-stage pipeline assets. AbbVie Stock Hits a Record After a 5.2% Dividend Raise: Why Its 276% Payout Ratio Doesn’t Tell the Entire Story
sum: - AbbVie raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $13.95 to $13.99 and lifted its quarterly dividend 5.2% to $1.82, as Skyrizi and Rinvoq sales each grew more than 22%.
- The GAAP payout ratio of 275.84% overstates the strain: the new $7.28 annual dividend uses about 52% of adjusted earnings, and Street estimates put that near 40% by 2028.
- The stock’s run to a record $294.89 has cut the forward yield to about 2.47%, which puts the focus on 2027 guidance at the fourth-quarter call.

AbbVie (ABBV) gave dividend investors the answer they were waiting for on Friday, October 30. Its third-quarter report showed revenue of $17.404 billion, up 10.3%, and adjusted EPS of $3.82. It also raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $13.95 to $13.99, from $13.76 to $13.96, and lifted the quarterly dividend 5.2% to $1.82 a share, starting with the February 16, 2027 payment.

Skyrizi and Rinvoq did the heavy lifting again. Skyrizi sales rose 22.7% to $5.776 billion and Rinvoq rose 23.9% to $2.706 billion, and on the earnings call management lifted their full-year targets to $21.8 billion and $10.3 billion. The stock closed at a record $294.89, up 1.4%.

In September, AbbVie stock’s 2.74% yield sat near a two-year low while its payout ratio looked stretched. The open question was simple: could earnings grow fast enough to fund another raise without the payout climbing further?

Friday’s numbers say yes. The headline doubling in Q3 adjusted EPS, from $1.86, is mostly a base effect: last year’s quarter carried a $1.50 charge for acquired R&D, against $0.11 this time. Strip that out of both quarters and adjusted EPS still rose about 17%, from $3.36 to $3.93. A 5.2% dividend increase is a small slice of that.

What Does AbbVie's (NYSE:ABBV) Drug-Pricing Deal Mean for the Stock?
sum: - The biopharma name joined the sweeping round of US pricing understandings under the most-favored-nation approach.
- Discounted cash prices on select medicines reach patients through a direct-to-consumer channel alongside Medicaid.
- A large multi-year domestic research and manufacturing commitment accompanies the broader agreement.

The company's agreement places it firmly within the industry-wide realignment that has defined the pharmaceutical space this season. Under the most-favored-nation approach, the group agreed to align certain domestic cash prices with the lower levels charged across other wealthy nations, joining a long procession of drugmakers that have reached similar understandings with the administration. In exchange for participating, the company secured relief from the branded import tariffs that had weighed on the sector, a trade that resolved a significant uncertainty for the group.

The pricing agreement intersects with this transition in notable ways. With the flagship medicine now facing biosimilar rivals and reaching patients through discounted channels, the economics of the franchise continue to evolve. How the company manages the balance between its maturing blockbuster and its growing successors is central to the market's reading of the name.

For the healthcare complex as a whole, the group serves as a barometer of how a large biopharma name manages the transition away from a historic blockbuster while adapting to a changing pricing environment.

A central feature of the company's agreement is the direct-to-consumer channel through which patients can obtain certain medicines at discounted cash prices. The arrangement extends to select immunology, ophthalmology, and metabolic treatments, offering cash-pay patients a more direct route to the medicines than the traditional system has allowed. For the company, the channel offers a way to serve patients who lack generous coverage, a group that has often struggled to afford branded medicines at their list prices. items.t: AbbVie Inc. (ABBV) Is a Trending Stock: Facts to Know Before Betting on It
sum: AbbVie (ABBV) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Over the past month, shares of this drugmaker have returned +10%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +1.6% change. During this period, the Zacks Large Cap Pharmaceuticals industry, which AbbVie falls in, has gained 2.9%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, AbbVie is expected to post earnings of $3.68 per share, indicating a change of +23.9% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +0.8% over the last 30 days.
The consensus earnings estimate of $14.23 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +42.3%. This estimate has changed -0.6% over the last 30 days.

items.t: AbbVie Inc Stock (ABBV) Moved Up by 3.44% on Jul 2: Drivers Behind the Movement
sum: AbbVie Inc (ABBV) moved up by 3.44%. The Pharmaceuticals & Medical Research sector is up by 2.35%. The company outperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Eli Lilly and Co (LLY) up 1.33%; Moderna Inc (MRNA) up 6.49%; Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) up 2.87%.

The primary catalyst driving the upward momentum and intraday volatility in AbbVie's stock is a sweeping regulatory development impacting the broader pharmaceutical sector. The Trump administration has proposed a new rule to modify reimbursement rates under the 340B Drug Pricing Program, aiming to curb hospital markups on outpatient medications. By capping how much hospitals can charge for discounted drugs, the policy shifts financial margins back in favor of major drug developers and away from hospital intermediaries. This policy alters the structural dynamics of the drug distribution market, igniting a strong rally across major pharmaceutical names and propelling AbbVie to a new 52-week high as investors anticipate enhanced margin retention for manufacturers.

Adding to this positive momentum is the highly favorable market reception to AbbVie's strategic acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics. While high-premium biotech acquisitions typically trigger short-term dilution concerns, Wall Street has reacted favorably to this deal. Analysts view the acquisition as a pivotal defensive expansion of AbbVie’s already dominant immunology franchise. By securing Apogee's promising clinical-stage pipeline, particularly in atopic dermatitis and asthma, the company is effectively building a secondary moat to sustain long-term revenue growth. This proactive portfolio diversification provides an attractive hedge against future patent expirations of legacy blockbusters.

Operational and pipeline execution have further bolstered investor confidence. AbbVie recently secured U.S. FDA approval for its blockbuster immunology drug, Skyrizi, to treat pediatric plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis. This milestone establishes it as the first and only drug of its class cleared for pediatric patients under a certain weight threshold, substantially widening its market reach.

Pharmaceutical Giant AbbVie Makes a Major Bet on a New Immunotherapy, and Its Dividend Growth Record Attracts Income-Focused Investors
sum: Recently, pharmaceutical giant AbbVie (ABBV) has demonstrated strong financial performance, driven primarily by its key growth engines, Skyrizi and Rinvoq. However, these two immunosuppressants will lose patent exclusivity within the next decade. Although the patent cliff is still some distance away, given the time required to develop entirely new therapies, now is an appropriate time for AbbVie to begin planning how to address this challenge. The company has recently taken a step in this direction through a large-scale acquisition. So, do these latest developments make AbbVie stock a worthy buy?

AbbVie faced difficulties in 2023 after its blockbuster autoimmune disease drug Humira lost U.S. patent exclusivity. However, the company offset the pressure with two newer immunology drugs, Skyrizi and Rinvoq, which are expected to generate combined sales exceeding $31 billion by 2027. Over the past three years, AbbVie has also invested more than $20 billion in acquisitions to diversify its product portfolio.

Since its spin-off from Abbott Laboratories (ABT) in 2013, AbbVie has raised its dividend every year. It currently offers a forward dividend yield of 2.7%, and over the past 12 months, dividends have consumed only 59% of free cash flow. Wall Street projects that, driven by Skyrizi and Rinvoq, expansion in the neuroscience business, stabilization of the oncology portfolio, and resilient sales of Botox (acquired through the Allergan purchase in 2019), AbbVie’s adjusted earnings per share will grow by 42% in 2026 and by 14% in 2027. At 18 times forward earnings, the stock still appears attractive in today’s red-hot market.

On June 22, AbbVie announced that it would acquire Apogee Therapeutics (APGE), a biotechnology company focused on developing drugs for immune and inflammatory diseases. AbbVie will pay approximately $10.9 billion in cash for this acquisition. In exchange, it will gain a pipeline containing multiple drug candidates, the most notable of which is zumilokibart, an investigational therapy for treating eczema. The drug has performed well in mid-stage studies and could fill an unmet medical need in this niche—many patients fail to achieve significant symptom improvement and continue to suffer from issues such as dry, itchy skin and plaques.

AbbVie vs. Pfizer: Which Pharma Giant Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
sum: Investors seeking reliable dividends often look to the healthcare sector, but choosing between AbbVie Inc (ABBV +1.06%) and Pfizer Inc (PFE -0.20%) requires a close look at their post-pandemic growth strategies and pipelines.

AbbVie focuses on high-margin specialty medicines in immunology and oncology, while Pfizer operates a broader portfolio spanning vaccines, primary care, and specialized cancer treatments. Both companies are navigating significant patent expirations, making their current research pipelines and acquisition strategies the primary drivers for long-term shareholder value in 2026.

AbbVie focuses on discovering and delivering innovative medicines for complex health issues through a global workforce of roughly 57,000 employees. Its U.S. pharmaceutical sales are heavily concentrated among three major wholesale distributors: McKesson Corporation (MCK -1.04%), Cardinal Health (CAH +1.46%), and Cencora (COR -1.80%). Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business because these three firms account for almost all domestic product sales.
In FY 2025, the company reported revenue of nearly $61.2 billion, representing growth of approximately 8.7% over the previous year. It achieved net income of roughly $4.3 billion during this period.
As of its most recent period, its debt level was $72.9 billion. During FY 2025, it generated more than $17.8 billion in free cash flow, defined as cash from operations minus capital expenditures.

Pfizer applies its global resources to develop and manufacture a wide range of vaccines and medicines for patients in roughly 200 countries. The company relies on a network of wholesale distributors and pharmacy chains, while government entities such as the CDC are critical customers of its vaccine products. It is currently focused on expanding its oncology footprint to diversify away from its legacy pharmaceutical stocks portfolio.

During FY 2025, Pfizer generated revenue of nearly $62.6 billion, representing a slight decline of approximately 1.6% from the previous fiscal year. Despite the dip in sales, it reported net income of close to $7.8 billion for the period.
